A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniAP. All pages, including appendices, provide readable text, equations, tables and figures. Corresponding material can be matched despite substantial reorganization and renamed hardware environments.

before.justification: v3 reports original throughput, strategy-optimization timing, scalability, ablation and estimation-accuracy results, including cloud-cluster experiments in Appendix G.

after.justification: v5 retains original empirical comparisons and analyses and adds Llama-7B scalability measurements on 16, 32 and 64 DCUs.

M1.justification: The profiling procedure, time and memory cost models, QIP/MIQP objectives and constraints, and unified optimization algorithm remain unchanged. Renaming pp_size to deg and disclosing platform-adapted libraries do not establish a changed optimization method.

E1.justification: v5 extends deployment scenarios to a 64-DCU cluster, beyond v3's 32-DCU cloud evaluation. Wikipedia, ImageNet-1K, task types and model families remain unchanged. The existing NVIDIA and DCU environments are otherwise consolidated or renamed.

E2.justification: Galvatron and Alpa remain the Table 1 comparators. Megatron and DeepSpeed remain in the cloud comparison, moved from v3 Table 4 to v5 Table 2. The added DCU scaling experiment introduces no comparator.

E3.justification: The added DCU scaling protocol uses FP32 Llama-7B with batches 2/4/8 on 16/32/64 DCUs; the retained cloud comparisons use FP16. Table 1 settings match after environment renaming. Unsuffixed EnvB references in v5's ablation and estimation passages leave their eight-versus-sixteen-GPU settings ambiguous and do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v5 adds a DCU scaling analysis and individual estimation-error points in Figure 8, supplementing v3's aggregate error comparison. The strategy-space ablation, BERT case study and Megatron candidate-strategy analysis are retained, with the latter moved into Section 4.4.

E5.justification: v3 Table 2 reports uncertainty for successful ablations, such as intra-only BERT throughput of 2.48 ± 0.02; v5 Figure 6 omits these uncertainty values. Other comparison tables retain the ± convention. Neither version specifies run counts, seeds or what those uncertainty values represent.

E6.justification: v5 Table 4 newly reports FP32 throughput of 0.1726, 0.3393 and 0.6656 samples/s on 16, 32 and 64 DCUs, with optimization times of 0.75, 1.64 and 1.55 minutes. All 18 main comparison rows, the existing cloud comparison and Megatron candidate statistics retain their values. These additions are not same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The contiguity theorem and proof, QIP/MIQP formulations and absolute relative-estimation-error definition are retained. Equation renumbering, pp_size-to-deg renaming and aligning the complexity expression's GPU symbol with n do not introduce substantive mathematical reasoning changes.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the first-joint-optimization claim and the reported improvements of up to 3.80× throughput and 107× strategy-optimization speed. Moving existing cloud results into the main text does not change these contributions.

C2.justification: v5 removes Appendix H's explicit qualification that UniAP is designed and tested for homogeneous clusters, leaving mixed NVIDIA/DCU clusters for future work. Section 4.4 also introduces a random-manual-choice interpretation of existing infeasible-strategy counts; the principal performance explanations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v5 adds disclosure of platform-adapted PyTorch and Megatron-DeepSpeed use, but omits v3 Appendix G's detailed DCU hardware specifications and exhaustive baseline-search timing procedure. The checklist's statement about supplementary MIQP code also disappears, without establishing actual withdrawal of code. Solver settings and most training details remain.

R1.justification: The citation to Wolf et al.'s Transformers paper, v3 reference 48, disappears with the checklist. The remaining cited works and the positioning of joint optimization against hierarchical parallelism are retained; reference renumbering is otherwise presentational.

P1.justification: v5 substantially reorganizes the narrative: Appendix A's explanation enters the method section, Appendix G's comparisons and analysis enter Sections 4.2 and 4.4, and estimation accuracy moves to Appendix E. The limitations, broader-impact section and checklist disappear. Much of the underlying method prose remains intact.

P2.justification: v5 adopts a two-column main text and references, resizes or redraws diagrams, and relocates cloud tables into the main text. It replaces the ablation table with Figure 6 and adds scaling Table 4 and estimation-error Figure 8. These substantially change the visual organization.

improvement.justification: v5 adds useful scaling evidence through 64 DCUs and makes existing cloud analyses more visible. However, omitting the detailed cloud hardware and baseline-timing procedure makes those comparisons harder to reproduce and assess, while the ablation loses uncertainty reporting. Figure 8 also plots negative errors despite retaining an absolute-error definition. These losses outweigh the limited added evidence without undermining the unchanged core method.
